note: Design quality is judged by people, not assertions. Run each prompt with and without the skill and compare the results side by side.

evals.name: landing-page-with-real-copy
evals.prompt: Make a landing page for Kiln & Co., a two-person ceramics studio in Hudson, NY. They sell small-batch tableware and run weekend wheel-throwing classes. Headline: 'Plates you'll hand down.' They have no reviews yet.
evals.expected_output: States a stance and constraint. Avoids the default SaaS layout. Includes no invented testimonials or review counts; any social-proof slot is clearly a placeholder. Body contrast and size meet the access check. Uses tokens for color and type.

evals.name: board-deck-from-notes
evals.prompt: Turn these notes into a 6-slide deck for our board: Q3 revenue $1.2M (up 18%), churn up from 3% to 4.1%, hired 2 engineers, launching the mobile app in November, need a decision on raising prices 10%.
evals.expected_output: One idea per slide with one dominant element. Uses only the given numbers, with nothing invented. The pricing decision is framed clearly. A restrained stance suited to a board audience. No decorative icons.

evals.name: poster-take-a-stance
evals.prompt: Poster for a noise-music night called STATIC FEAST at a warehouse venue, Oct 31, 10pm, $12 at the door. Go bold.
evals.expected_output: Commits to a named expressive stance with an explicit constraint. Legible at poster distance. Keeps all the event facts correct and gives them clear hierarchy. Delivers one recommendation, not several variations.

evals.name: single-change-request
evals.prompt: (After a design exists) Make the headline shorter; everything else is perfect.
evals.expected_output: Changes only the headline and preserves the layout, colors, and all other copy.

evals.name: honest-critique
evals.prompt: Critique this SaaS homepage: centered hero with a purple-blue gradient, 'Unlock the power of AI for your team', three feature cards with emoji icons, a logo bar of 'trusted by' companies.
evals.expected_output: Names the median pattern specifically, questions whether the logo bar is real, and recommends one clear direction with the reasoning, rather than a list of small tweaks.
